git_basics.notes: Maintained expert level. Continued application of Git fundamentals in branching context. Demonstrated fluency with repository operations while learning advanced branching concepts.

terminal_comfort.notes: Maintained proficient level. Executed complex command sequences for branch operations, created git aliases, navigated between branches with confidence.

markdown_documentation.notes: Created comprehensive README.md with proper markdown formatting (headers, lists, code blocks). Documented project vision, features, tech stack professionally. Portfolio-ready documentation skills.

project_organization.notes: Maintained competent level. Applied branching workflow to organize feature development. Understanding of how branches support organized parallel development for complex projects.

technical_vocabulary.notes: Maintained proficient level. Expanded vocabulary with branching concepts: branch pointer, HEAD pointer, detached HEAD, feature branch, hotfix branch, bugfix branch, checkout, switch, upstream tracking, branch divergence, commit graph, parallel development. Clear understanding of technical distinctions (git checkout vs git switch, git branch vs git checkout -b, -d vs -D flags).

systems_thinking.notes: Advanced from competent to proficient. Exceptional demonstration of meta-level systems thinking: identified curriculum structure flaws, recognized proper role separation (Architect vs Professor), proposed architectural improvements affecting entire 28-phase curriculum. Understanding of how system design impacts learning outcomes. Professional-level awareness of scalability implications (140+ modules).

commit_message_writing.notes: Maintained expert level. Continued application of Conventional Commits format in branching context. Understanding of how commit messages relate to branch naming conventions and issue tracking integration.

github_workflow.notes: Maintained proficient level. Applied branching concepts with understanding of how they'll integrate with GitHub pull requests (upcoming in P01-M02-L02). Ready for collaborative GitHub workflows.

ssh_authentication.notes: Already had SSH configured from previous work (The Odin Project, dev-curriculum). Excellent understanding of ssh-agent purpose, SSH vs HTTPS tradeoffs, and Personal Access Token distinctions. Professional-level authentication setup. Ready for advanced scenarios (multiple SSH keys, SSH config management).

remote_repository_management.notes: Maintained proficient level. Understanding of how branches integrate with remote repositories (origin/main, remote branch tracking). Ready for push/pull operations with feature branches.

multi_device_sync.notes: Excellent visualization of two-computer workflow (pull → work → commit → push → repeat). Understands importance of pulling before starting work to avoid conflicts. Ready for real-world multi-device CatchBook development scenarios.

atomic_commits.notes: Maintained expert level. Applied atomic commit principles in feature branch context. Understanding that branches isolate logical features while individual commits within branches remain atomic.

git_history_navigation.notes: Maintained expert level. Extended mastery to branch visualization with git log --graph --all --oneline --decorate. Created git lg alias independently and verified functionality. Complete understanding of how to navigate multi-branch repositories.

gitignore_configuration.notes: Proactively created .gitignore during L02 bonus challenge, enhanced with comprehensive patterns in L04. Understands why files should be ignored (secrets, dependencies, build artifacts, OS files, IDE configs). Correct pattern syntax knowledge. Excellent understanding of git rm --cached for retroactive exclusion. Strong security awareness—immediately recognized API key prevention as critical use case. Portfolio-ready repository hygiene.

security_awareness.notes: Maintained competent level. Applied security thinking to branch naming (avoiding overly detailed vulnerability descriptions in public repos). Understanding that branches provide isolation for security-sensitive work.

git_branching.notes: NEW SKILL. Exceptional mastery of Git branching concepts: branches as pointers (not copies), HEAD pointer behavior, branch creation (git branch vs git checkout -b vs git switch -c), branch naming conventions (feature/, bugfix/, hotfix/), branch listing (git branch -v, -a, -vv), branch visualization (git log --graph), detached HEAD understanding, branch deletion (-d vs -D). Independently discovered professional practices (ticket number integration). Successfully created feature branch for CatchBook and verified isolation. Created git lg alias and demonstrated practical workflow application. Ready for advanced branching topics (merge strategies, conflict resolution, rebase).

command_line_fluency.notes: NEW SKILL. Demonstrated proficient command-line skills: executed complex Git commands with multiple flags, created global git config aliases, switched between branches, verified working directory state changes, interpreted ASCII graph output. Comfortable with terminal-based workflows and troubleshooting.

professional_workflow_patterns.notes: NEW SKILL. Understanding of professional development workflows: feature branch workflow, branch naming conventions matching industry standards (feature/, bugfix/, hotfix/), issue tracking integration (ticket numbers in branch names), isolation of experimental work, workflow efficiency (git aliases). Ready to apply these patterns throughout CatchBook development across 28 phases.
